newsitem.title: USA: US comptroller recused from NationsBank issue.
newsitem.headline: US comptroller recused from NationsBank issue.

text.p: Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig has recused himself from consideration of a historic request from NationsBank Corp for expanded powers, the comptroller's office said Thursday.
Ludwig feared his participation in the decision would be tainted by a NationsBank executive's attendance at a controversial White House coffee last May, the comptroller said in a statement.
"To ensure there can be no question about the integrity of the decision process, I am recusing myself from involvement in the decisions on these two applications," Ludwig said.

"Given the notoriety of the May 13, 1996 meeting with bankers at the White House and because the two NationsBank applications for operating subsidiaries are the first of this type received by the Comptroller's Office, there must be absolutely no question of the impartiality and fairness of the decision on these applications," Ludwig said.

NationsBank CEO Hugh McColl attended a coffee with other bank executives at the White House attended by President Bill Clinton, Ludwig and other bank regulators. Ludwig said later he did not realize the event was sponsored by the Democratic National Committee and would not have attended had he known.
Some of the banks whose executives attended the meeting, including NationsBank, gave substantial campaign contributions to Clinton's re-election effort.

NationsBank, in two March 26 applications, was the first financial institution to ask the comptroller for authority to establish a direct subsidiary that will not be a bank under a new rule adopted last November.
Under the rule, banks may ask permisssion on a case-by-case basis to set up direct subsidiaries to engage in non-banking activities not previously permitted.

NationsBank, the fourth largest bank in the country, asked for permission to create real estate development and real estate leasing subsidiaries. The Comptroller's office is accepting comments on the applications for 60 days before rendering a decision.
Ludwig said the decision on the Nationsbank applications would be made by the agency's chief counsel, Julie Williams.
Ludwig has not recused himself from other matters pertaining to NationsBank or the other banks that attended the White House coffee, spokeswoman Lee Cross said.

"The comptroller was concerned about this decision, the first one, that there would be no questions," Cross said. "But for all other matters relating to NationsBank or the other banks, he's still the comptroller."
The comptroller's recusal was first reported in Thursday's edition of the Washington Post.
Rep Spencer Bachus, the Alabama Republican who heads a subcommittee overseeing the comptroller's office, said Ludwig's recusal was proper.

"In light of the questions surrounding the fund-raising coffee at the White House held last May that the comptroller attended, this is an appropriate action," Bachus said. "Mr Ludwig has exercised good judgement in this instance and I commend him."
